I wish I could give this an honest review of a 4 or a 5, because I know that the people who put it there were trying to solve a universal problem and had a kind heart. However, it must be noted that maintenence was a huge issue. It was completely covered in graffiti. It was completely unclean, with tissues all over the place. Lights in the small box were years away- it was completely dark. Although the flush was operative, the hand washing station was not. It was seeming that nobody had the responsibility of cleaning this place, as it was clear that it had not been cleaned in days, if not weeks.
If possible, steer clear of their restroom, and find a local shop.

text:
Harvard Square never disappoints! I recently took my aunt for a visit, and we had such a lovely time soaking in the atmosphere. One of our favorite stops was the The Harvard Coop—and of course, we couldn’t leave without picking up some merchandise!

What made this visit extra special was how surprisingly uncrowded it was. We were able to stroll comfortably, browse at our own pace, and truly enjoy the charm of the Square without the usual hustle and bustle.

It’s always such a classic Boston experience—great shopping, beautiful surroundings, and that unmistakable Harvard vibe. A must-visit every time!

text:
We were lucky enough to have our wedding reception at State Park and truly could not have imagined a better experience. Chelsea was incredible to work with. She always available to answer our questions, and so helpful in planning the flow of the night. She made the entire process feel easy and stress-free.

The night of the wedding, Nicholas managed everything seamlessly and kept the evening running so smoothly behind the scenes so we could actually relax and enjoy ourselves. The bartenders absolutely crushed it. Every drink was amazing and they somehow kept the bar moving incredibly fast all night long.

Every single guest commented on how amazing the food was and how much fun they had. We’re still hearing about it weeks later. State Park created the perfect atmosphere for our reception and exceeded every expectation we had. We are so grateful to the entire team for making our wedding night feel so special. Highly, highly recommend!

text: Do residents of Cambridge vote for the stuff forced upon you? Number one, please read the drawbacks to the place based treaty. They are real…but if your constituents want it, then far be it from me to complain. Also, I can’t imagine riding a bike home from work after being on my feet from 6am to 5pm. Are any of the commuting bike riders blue collar? I’m not from your area so moving here was a shock. Are the bike lanes something that a majority of the people in your town want or was it forced upon them? I avoid your city while staying in Belmont (wild how far I’m willing to drive around to avoid) because it’s a standstill with no lanes. (Except for Phil’s awesome twenty dollar haircuts. I’ll always deal with traffic for his place) Do you want your city to have no conservative or poor ppl living there? That seems like a recipe for failure of a tax base in such a dense area

text: Kresge Auditorium reminds me of a wedge of an egg. The interior and exterior are beautiful.  The acoustics are clear inside the auditorium.  There is a whispering gallery.  You can go to one end inside and whisper and a person at the other end of the gallery can hear you distinctly.  There is no other building that looks like Kresge.  You can sit or lie on the base of the building outside or try to climb it -- you won't get far.  One of the great mysteries is the lack of elevators or accessibility for people with physical limitations.  The restrooms are in the basement which are around 18 steps and there is a lift for final three stairs, but why not put a lift for the other 15 steps?  Basically, for people with issues with steps, you need to climb stairs to get into the Auditorium, you need to walk down stairs for the Little Kresge Theatre, and the most steps are to the restrooms.  Eero Saarinen the architect was probably able-bodied and didn't think beyond aesthetics and acoustics.

text: Caspar, the shelter at 240 albany, feeds people donuts for breakfast and low quality, nutrient poor foods. They have a nice restaurant grade kitchen, too. Also, they refused my donation of two loaves of bread, two cartons of eggs, and three cartons of strawberries purchased via food stamps. I don't necessarily disagree with their decision to refuse the food, but there is CLEARLY some abuse of power happening here. People, please investigate this situation and take action so that the people living in the shelter can eat healthily. Share it on social media. Also, build a 5 star hotel resort for the homeless, and rezone the golf course.

And then later that evening after spending most of the night inside the bar, I asked the patio staff for 4 of us to eat on the patio, where he said yes, but then when I went to collect the rest of the group in the bar, the bar staff told me we were not allowed to go up to the patio. So then I had to wait while those two connected on the issue. We then ate up there, no problem. Anyway, didn’t enjoy the tension.

text:
This place is exactly what you want out of a dive. Good vibe, warm atmosphere, no frills, and surprisingly good food. Food punches well above its weight for a place like this. Beer list is pleasant, with several options (national, local, and import).

Duck nachos are awesome because each chip is loaded so your bite is perfect. The kale Cesar is surprisingly good (I’m not a salad guy). Wings looked better than they tasted and were admittedly average (think they could have used a few more min in the fryer), as was the sandwich, but overall I was pleased with everything we got.
